messages:
Evelyn Park: Hi all, excited to join! Quick onboarding snag: my monitor shipment shows 'out for delivery' since yesterday but tracking stopped updating. Also dock arrived but when I plug in laptop the external monitor shows 'No Signal' and the corporate Wi-Fi cert prompt never popped during setup. Can someone advise before I open a ticket?

Jamie (IT Support): Welcome, @Evelyn :tada: Sorry about the rough start. Quick questions: 1) Which laptop model? 2) Are you using HDMI or DisplayPort from the dock? 3) Can you paste the exact VPN/corp-wifi error text? We can try quick troubleshooting before a ticket.

Evelyn Park: Laptop is Dell XPS 13 (Intel). Dock is the standard company USB4 dock. I tried HDMI on the dock and the monitor (HP 27f) just goes to 'No Signal'. VPN error says: "Certificate not found for user authentication". I didn't see any cert install prompt.

Jamie (IT Support): Thanks. Try these quick steps: 1) Power-cycle the dock (unplug power, wait 10s, plug back). 2) Swap to the DP port if available. 3) Try the laptop's native USB-C -> monitor cable directly (bypass dock). 4) For the cert: open Edge/Chrome and go to https://onboard.redwood.example/cert-install and follow the mac/win installer. If that page errors, paste the screenshot. If any of those fail, I'll file IT ticket and request rapid replacement dock if needed.

Evelyn Park: Power cycled dock, swapped DP (no change). Direct USB-C -> HDMI cable to monitor worked immediately (so monitor fine, dock seems to be the passthrough). I tried the cert installer page and it started but ended with "installer failed: 0x80070005".

Jamie (IT Support): Good debug, that narrows it to dock passthrough and installer permission issue. For the installer failure 0x80070005 is an access denied on Windows. Try running the installer as Administrator: right-click -> Run as administrator. Also open Device Manager > Firmware Update Services and see if the dock shows under 'USB devices' with any warning icons. I'll create a ticket to track replacement dock & escalate the cert installer failure.

Logistics Bot: Shipment ID SH-7724 for monitor (HP 27f) updated: delivery delayed due to carrier reroute. New ETA: 2 business days. Contact logistics-team for expedited handling.

Evelyn Park: Ran the installer as admin; it progressed further but then asked to trust a company certificate and I clicked 'Install' and now VPN shows authenticated but corp-wifi still fails to connect with "802.1X: Authentication failed". I can join the guest network for now.

Jamie (IT Support): If VPN authenticated that's good. For 802.1X, check that the machine has the right user cert installed: run certmgr.msc and look under Personal -> Certificates for one issued to your username. If it's missing, the installer may have only installed the VPN cert. Paste a screenshot if unsure. I'll attach IT-2218 to this thread and set P2. We'll ship out a replacement dock tomorrow AM and a powered USB hub as a backup.

Omar (Facilities): @Evelyn sorry about the monitor ETA. If you need a temporary monitor, we have a handful in the SF office spare closet. I can drop one with your name if you're local, or we can expedite courier if remote.

Evelyn Park: Thanks everyone. I'm remote Bay Area, courier would be great if possible. I can check certmgr and send screenshot in a bit. Appreciate the quick responses!

Jamie (IT Support): Copy that. IT-2218 created by Jamie (IT Support) for Evelyn Park — "Dock passthrough failure + Wi-Fi 802.1X auth + monitor delivery delay". Priority: P2. ETA triage: 2 hours. Tracking: replacement dock & hub to ship tomorrow.

Evelyn Park: Updated: certmgr shows a user cert issued to me under Personal, and VPN now connects reliably. Still need dock replacement for passthrough but guest wifi works for now. Thanks :heart:
